newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Alliance would boost SIA, Air NZ, Ansett - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Alliance would boost SIA, Air NZ, Ansett - analysts.

text.p: The proposed alliance of Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA), Air New Zealand and Australia's Ansett International would benefit all three carriers, analysts said on Monday.
SIA confirmed on Monday it had held talks with the other two companies over a possible "commercial relationship".
It said in a statement that it regularly explored commercial opportunities "near and far", and stressed that such discussions sometimes came to nothing.

But analysts said the fact that SIA saw fit to issue a statement, confirming some facets of a report in the Australian Financial Review earlier on Monday, suggested the alliance might be in the wings.
"Such an alliance would be very interesting to SIA," said Christopher Chong, head of research at HSBC James Capel in Singapore. "Anything that outflanks Qantas is good for them."

Breaking the news of the discussions, the usually well-sourced Australian daily said a tie-up between the three carriers would pose a threat to the linkup of Qantas Airways and British Airways Plc on routes between Australia and Europe.
Analysts agreed, saying airline operations on such major passenger routes benefited greatly from the code-sharing and freer access that alliances could offer.

Chong said SIA in particular would gain from a relationship with Air New Zealand and Ansett, which is a 50/50 joint venture of News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand, by getting access to more Australian cities.
"This could give them more Australia destinations and enable them to make good use of their new Boeing 777 aircraft, due to be delivered from this year," he said.
The Boeing 777 is ideally suited to medium-distance routes, such as those in Australia, he said.
Other analysts said they wanted to know more about the potential alliance before assessing the possible benefits.

SIA's statement was thin on detail. "In this case, we can only confirm that discussions have taken place with Ansett and Air New Zealand on a commercial relationship. It is premature to speculate on the outcome of such discussions," it said.
"We shall not disclose any further details until we are ready to do so," the statement added.
Another analyst, who declined to be identified, said a tie-up between the three companies could help improve load factors on the Europe-Singapore-Australasia route.
These were already good at between 70 and 75 percent, but an improvement would help counter the rising cost of fuel, he said.
"Air NZ would presumably have access to SIA's destinations beyond Singapore," said the analyst. "Air NZ is not particularly well-positioned in geographical terms. This would help them."

Last week's announcement of an open skies agreement between Singapore and the United States would also make an alliance with SIA more attractive to any carrier, since it offered potentially unlimited access to U.S. cities.
"If this comes off, I wouldn't expect it to have an immediate impact on SIA's bottom line. But eventually it would be positive. It will take time," said Chong.
